To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Old Saybrook and Madison end moraines extend farther westward than previously known and that a probable westward extension of the Old Saybrooke moraine has been identified by acoustic-reflection studies of the bottom of Long Island Sound.

the late Wisconsin Laurentide ice sheet extended southward along the Connecticut coast, that it was grounded in the area between New Haven and Old Saybrook and that it advanced to the sea at a later time than previously thought.

(1) the Old Saybrook and Madison moraines are end moraines of the late Wisconsin Laurentide Ice Sheet; (2) the Old Say Brook moraine is the more easterly of the two and extends offshore to the south of the Connecticut River; (3) the Old Saybrooke moraine is the older of the two, and the Madison moraines is the younger, as evidenced by the presence of the former on bedrock and the absence of the latter on bedrock;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the late Wisconsin Laurentide Ice Sheet and the glacial history of southern New England.
the identification and correlation of end moraines in southern New England, and the recognition of their probable offshore continuations.

the identification of end moraines, the recognition and interpretation of ice-contact stratified deposits, and the determination of the position and character of the ice sheet margin during the Wisconsin glaciation.

the ice sheet was not as large as previously believed.
the late Wisconsin ice sheet reached the Connecticut coast at least twice, and possibly three or four times.
the late Wisconsin ice sheet in Connecticut reached a position of maximum advance about 20 km inland from the present coast, and that it retreated to the present coast in two or more steps.

, in this region of southern New England, a major late Wisconsin glacier margin was located about 50 km from the coast and that the glacier was active for a period of about 1000 years, during which it was in contact with a marine environment.
the late Wisconsin Laurentide Ice Sheet reached a maximum extent of about 100 km from the coast in the vicinity of the Old Saybrooke moraine.
the late Wisconsin ice sheet was not a single entity, as has often been supposed, but a complex of separate and interacting ice masses, each of which had its own history and its own characteristics.

the Laurentide Ice Sheet was more dynamic than previously thought.
